newsitem.title: UK: UK government delays decision on M25 widening.
newsitem.headline: UK government delays decision on M25 widening.

text.p: The British government said on Monday it was delaying a decision on a proposed widening of the M25 London orbital motorway near Heathrow airport.
Transport Minister Gavin Strang gave the go-ahead for five other key projects, including a northern relief road for Birmingham.
But he scrapped plans for a by-pass around the city of Salisbury, which campaigners said would spoil the view of the tallest cathedral spire in England.
The 85 million stg M25 plan would have widened the road between junctions 12 and 15 to a maximum of six lanes per carriageway.

Other projects which Strang said he would need more time to consider are design, build, finance and operate (DBFO) works on roads linking Bradford and Cumbria, work on the M62 (East) and M606 link roads, and two more DBFO projects, one in the South Midlands and the other in the Hastings area.
Other schemes which will go ahead are the A13 Thames Gateway DBFO, the Denton-Middleton contract for the M66, the Derby southern by-pass and the M2-A2 widening scheme.
Strang also scrapped the A40 West London approach DBFO project.
